# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 - Summary

## Economic Vision

The manifesto centres on economic stability following COVID-19 and the Ukraine crisis, highlighting reduced inflation, rising real wages, and restored growth. The Conservatives pledge to maintain fiscal discipline while cutting taxes, having already reduced National Insurance and planning to halve it from 12% to 6% by April 2027 for employees. Self-employed workers would see their main rate of National Insurance abolished entirely. The party commits to not raising income tax, VAT, or corporation tax.

## Tax and Family Support

The "Triple Lock Plus" guarantees State Pensions and pensioner tax allowances rise by the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%. Child Benefit reforms would introduce a household-based system, with families only losing benefits when combined income reaches £120,000. Working parents would receive 30 hours of free childcare weekly from when children are nine months old.

## Immigration and Border Security

A legally binding migration cap would be introduced, with numbers falling annually. The Rwanda removal policy would continue with regular deportation flights. The party pledges to reform asylum rules internationally and sign further returns agreements. Illegal migrants would be prevented from staying in the UK.

## Defence and Security

Defence spending would increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, representing the largest sustained increase since the Cold War. The manifesto emphasises continued support for Ukraine and strengthening NATO commitments.

## Public Services

NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with plans for 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors. Technology investments totalling £3.4 billion would modernise healthcare delivery. Housing targets aim for 1.6 million new homes, with stamp duty abolished for first-time buyers on homes up to £425,000.

## Young People and Education

Mandatory National Service would be introduced for 18-year-olds, offering either military placement or civic volunteering. The party promises 100,000 new apprenticeships funded by closing poor-performing university courses, alongside mobile phone bans in schools.

## Energy and Environment

The approach to net zero emphasises pragmatism, with continued North Sea oil and gas licensing, nuclear expansion including Small Modular Reactors, and trebled offshore wind capacity. Green levies would be kept lower than 2023 levels.
